transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Khatri (CSM), Diego Ramos (SE); Maya Chen (Evergreen Head of AI), Ravi Singh (CTO), Elena Park (DevOps), Samir Patel (Security), Jordan Lee (Product)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff to align onboarding milestones, network/security requirements, staging tests, and SE deep dive to map data flows. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, VPC options, KMS, SSO, and basic success criteria for pilot.

Topics:
- Onboarding timeline and milestones
- Network & security (VPC, KMS, SSO, audit logs)
- Staging API keys and test plan
- Roles and RACI for implementation
- Next steps and handoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, we have Priya and Diego with me, Priya will be your CSM and Diego is the solutions engineer who will help with the technical deep dive. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: Good, thanks Alex, excited to get started. quick note, sorry if the audio's a bit fuzzy on my end.
[00:18] Ravi: yep, we're all here. our timeline is a little tight—want to hit a pilot in Q2.
[00:24] Alex: Great, we'll aim to align. Today we want to confirm success criteria, network/security needs, initial test plan, and owners. Diego will sketch the technical steps.
[00:35] Diego: cool, i'll keep it practical. quick preface: Evergreen, is the pilot mostly internal tool integration or customer-facing?
[00:42] Jordan: internal first, then customer facing. primary use is clinical summarization and internal triage, so PHI considerations are relevant.
[00:52] Samir: yes security is top priority. we need encryption at rest and in transit, audit logs, SOC2 evidence, and we also have a corporate KMS for key management.
[01:05] Priya: noted, Samir. Redwood supports hosted and private options—our hosted API can be used with strong retention controls and optional enterprise KMS, but for PHI most customers choose Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) to meet compliance.
[01:21] Maya: can you clarify the difference? i.e., what changes operationally between hosted and dedicated?
[01:26] Diego: yeah so hosted is our multi-tenant API with strict data controls; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and tenancy for isolation, Private (VPC) places the control plane in your VPC or on-prem depending on the package. With Dedicated you still get Redwood operational support and SLAs but you can pin models, autoscale policies, and have network egress controls.
[01:47] Ravi: if we go Dedicated or Private, how does KMS integration work? we have keys in AWS KMS and want to ensure customer-managed keys.
[01:55] Diego: we integrate with customer KMS via standard IAM roles and an HSM bridge where needed. For Private, keys remain in your VPC/HSM; for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations with customer-managed keys in most regions. we'll need specific ARN and admin contact—Elena, that will be you.
[02:11] Elena: yep i'll pull ARNs and what network appliances we use. also, what about IP allowlist and VPN?
[02:17] Alex: we'll capture that in the integration checklist. typical asks: static egress IPs, SAML SSO for the console, and optionally a VPN or private link. Diego, do we have a doc with required ports and IPs?
[02:29] Diego: i do, i'll share the network reqs doc. it has sample AWS VPC peering, private link, and port lists. i'll include S3 permissions notes for model artifacts and KV cache persistence paths (note: KV cache is handled in runtime, we can persist some states depending on config).
[02:45] Maya: great — for the pilot we need latency under 400ms p50 for short summaries and costs under our budgeted cap. we want to avoid surprises.
[02:55] Priya: we'll capture those as pilot success criteria—latency target, throughput, and a quality rubric for summaries. we'll also run a small benchmark in staging to validate.
[03:05] Ravi: on that benchmark, what's the typical approach? are you running against Redwood verified models or do we bring our own?
[03:12] Diego: we recommend starting with a Redwood-curated open model for parity, then if you want to bring a custom fine-tuned model we can onboard it—for the pilot we'll do 1000 sample calls with your prompt set, measure latency, throughput, token costs, and quality metrics.
[03:28] Samir: is there any on-prem option for air-gapped? some of our clinics need isolated deployments.
[03:34] Alex: yes we have a Private on-prem package, it's more involved but feasible. Diego will outline the high-level steps and timeline.
[03:41] Diego: on-prem generally needs a week or two for infra prep depending on customer stack—we'll need access to networking, storage, and the local infra team for cert installs.
[03:49] Jordan: ok that's fine, but for pilot we'll stay hosted/Dedicated. if pilot hits criteria we'll evaluate Private next quarter.
[03:56] Alex: perfect. next operational items—SSO and RBAC. are you using Okta?
[04:01] Maya: yes Okta and we also use SCIM for user provisioning.
[04:05] Priya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM. Diego will help with the SSO test plan.
[04:12] Diego: quick note on logging: we emit audit logs and you can ship them to your SIEM; retention is configurable for enterprise plans. Samir, we'll want to confirm retention window and export format.
[04:24] Samir: we prefer daily exports to S3 and a 7-year retention for audit artifacts, but for pilot 1 year is ok. we'll confirm.
[04:33] Alex: on the timeline—our recommended milestones: onboarding doc + integration checklist within 48 hours, SE deep-dive within 5 business days, staging keys and sample tests within 7 days, and pilot results within 4 weeks. Does that align?
[04:47] Ravi: that tracks. who owns the staging key setup?
[04:51] Diego: Diego and Elena pair on that—Diego will provision initial staging keys from the console and Elena will check VPC/firewall rules. we'll also provide a postman collection and sample prompts.
[05:02] Maya: can you include an example prompt set for clinical summaries? we have some legacy prompts, but we want Redwood's guidance on prompt engineering.
[05:10] Priya: absolutely, we'll include a prompt pack and a suggested eval rubric. also we'll attach any relevant docs: SOC2 summary, PCI/PHI notes, and our standard BAA.
[05:21] Jordan: curious, are you seeing any major differences in token cost between your open models and bigger proprietary ones? we want to keep costs predictable.
[05:28] Diego: cost varies by model and quantization; we can recommend lighter-weight quantized variants for chat-like tasks. Redwood Optimize will give recommendations based on workload—batching, caching and quantization choices can reduce unit cost significantly.
[05:41] Maya: cool. one more question: will we get access to the Console for metrics and per-route dashboards during the pilot?
[05:48] Alex: yes, we'll grant a console staging account with limited access; Priya will set up roles.
[05:54] Priya: i'll provision the workspace and send invites after SSO is configured.
[06:00] Ravi: anything else on the legal side? our procurement team will need pricing and the BAA.
[06:06] Alex: i'll send the pricing addendum and BAA as part of the onboarding packet.
[06:10] Maya: awesome.
[06:15] Diego: recap of technical next steps so we don't miss anything: 1) share network/IP list and KMS ARN 2) set up staging API keys 3) run 1k sample calls with your prompt pack 4) collect latency/cost/quality metrics.
[06:29] Alex: great, let's call out owners and dates—(we did this in action log). any other blockers?
[06:34] Elena: i'll need a short list of required IAM permissions and if you need an S3 bucket created.
[06:39] Diego: i'll include an S3 permissions snippet and minimal IAM policy in the network doc.
[06:45] Samir: security team will review the BAA and SOC2 docs, expect comments next week.
[06:51] Priya: perfect, we have alignment. we'll send the onboarding doc by Friday.
[06:56] Alex: ok thanks everyone—closing notes: Alex to send onboarding doc and pricing addendum; Diego to schedule SE deep-dive; Maya to share prompts and dataflow; Elena to confirm network and KMS info. we'll reconvene after the deep-dive. Thanks!
[07:10] Maya: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Recap / Next steps (brief):
- Redwood to send onboarding packet (docs, pricing, BAA) by 2026-03-06.
- SE deep dive scheduled (target week of 2026-03-09) to map VPC/KMS/SSO.
- Customer to provide: sample prompts, dataflow diagram, KMS ARNs and network firewall rules by 2026-03-08.
- Staging keys and initial smoke tests targeted by 2026-03-10.

Notes: transcription contains minor speech recognition errors and some product names may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache spelled out in conversation).
